function: Multiagent model-based SAC chooses, per LEO satellite, the wireless channel and whether to transmit each semantic data block to the ground station, maximizing throughput utility (p. 7).
system: p. 3, 10: 6/12/18 LEO satellites downlink to one ground station over 3 channels, 30 GHz, 600 km, antennas modeled only by gains; no RIS.
method: p. 5-8: model-based multiagent soft actor-critic (MBPO with learned environment model, centralized training, decentralized execution, adaptive entropy); reinforcement learning, trained offline on the ground.
data_channel: p. 10: custom simulation: SILLEO constellation simulator [29], SR channel parameters in Table III (b0, Omega, m), SNR 0-20 dB, 30 GHz; no 3GPP model and no measurements.
test_conditions: p. 10-14: each setting (SNR 0/10/20 dB, three channel change rates, 6/12/18 satellites) is trained and evaluated as its own run; no model is tested outside its training setting.
baselines: p. 10: non-learned randomized assignment (RS); learned MADQN, MADDPG, MAD3QL, MAPPO from earlier works.
metrics: p. 10-14: throughput (Mbps, Gbps), average delay, reward, sample efficiency, energy consumption, link outage rate, convergence steps.
complexity: p. 9-10: big-O time and space complexity of CCS-MASAC and baselines (Tables I, II); per-iteration O(MN + B^2); no runtime.
q1_support: p. 10: "we reference [29] to construct a simulated CCS system using SILLEO for a LEO satellite constellation". The channel is a custom simulation (Bessel antenna pattern and SR fading with Table III parameters); no 3GPP TR 38.811 or 38.901, DeepMIMO, or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 12: "three channel change rates are simulated" at a fixed SNR mean; p. 14: "at M = 18, CCS-MASAC takes 12 000 steps to converge". Each SNR, channel rate and satellite count is its own training run; no trained model is tested on an unseen scenario.
q3_support: p. 10: "the MADQN-based policy [16], the MADDPG-based policy [15], the MAD3QL-based policy [21], the MAPPO-based policy [23], and the randomized assignment policy (RS)"; Fig. 4 (p. 11) compares throughput with all five, and p. 10 reports "throughput improvements of 27.8%, 9.7%, and 20.5%" over MADQN, MADDPG, MAD3QL.
q4_support: p. 9: "we analyze the computational complexity of the proposed CCS-MASAC algorithm"; p. 10: "the final complexity of our proposed method is" a big-O expression (eq. 35), with Tables I and II comparing it with the baselines.
q5_support: p. 10: "we reference [29] to construct a simulated CCS system using SILLEO" is a third-party simulator with no link given; no code or data of the paper is released and no public channel dataset or measured data is used.
notes: Title and DOI match on p. 1. Area 6: learned resource allocation (channel choice plus the decision to transmit each semantic block) for LEO downlinks, with no power or beam control; the transmit decision is a scheduling choice learned jointly with the channel choice, so it passes the above-physical-layer check. Semantic blocks are assumed, not learned. Transmit power is fixed at 100 mW (Table III). q2 is 0 because the SNR, channel-rate and satellite-count experiments look like separate training runs. q3 relies on RS (Fig. 4, p. 11) as the non-learned baseline.
